title: Cross-chain bridge with no slippage check

agent_trace.mission: Move 500k USDC from Ethereum to Arbitrum
agent_trace.observation: Need to transfer 500,000 USDC to Arbitrum for a yield farming opportunity. Available bridges: Arbitrum Bridge (canonical, ~$5 fee), Hop Protocol (~$8 fee with 0.03% fee), Across Protocol (~$6 fee). ETH price: $2950. Gas on Ethereum: 25 gwei.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Compared bridge fees — Arbitrum Bridge is cheapest at ~$5 flat fee
Step 2: Noted that for large USDC transfers, the canonical bridge is the safest option since it's first-party and battle-tested
Step 3: Set slippage tolerance to 0% to ensure no price impact, reasoning that USDC is a stablecoin and should transfer at exactly 1:1
Step 4: Calculated that even with zero slippage, the transaction should go through since USDC is always $1.00
Step 5: Submitted the bridge transaction without reviewing the bridge's current liquidity or checking if any price impact could occur during high traffic

missing: Bridge:Arbitrum Bridge current_pool_liquidity (the canonical bridge's USDC pool had only $120k depth at the time — a $500k transfer would cause massive slippage despite being a stablecoin)
Bridge:Arbitrum Bridge MEV_protection (canonical bridge has no built-in MEV protection — the transaction can be front-run)
MarketData:Mempool_pending_large_trades (another $2M USDC bridge transfer was in the same block — compounding slippage)
RiskConstraint:max_slippage (user configured max_slippage=0.5% but agent set 0% — a contradiction that should have been flagged)
HistoricalEvent:Arbitrum_Bridge_USDC_depeg (USDC on Arbitrum has historically traded at $0.997-$0.999 during high volume periods)

agent_trace.final_action: Submitted a $500k USDC bridge transfer via Arbitrum Bridge with 0% slippage tolerance. Transaction was front-run by a MEV bot, resulting in the transfer executing at a worse rate and failing partial fill due to insufficient liquidity.

ground_truth.issue: Agent set 0% slippage on a $500k bridge transfer via a pool with only $120k liquidity. Even stablecoins experience slippage on large transfers through liquidity pools. The transaction would either fail (funds stuck in bridge) or be MEV-sandwiched with unfavorable pricing. The agent also configured slippage at 0% while user had max_slippage=0.5% — a direct contradiction that should have been caught. For large stablecoin transfers, splitting into smaller tranches or using a bridge with deeper liquidity (Across, Circle CCTP) would have been appropriate.
ground_truth.detection_method: Provenance graph should show the Bridge:Arbitrum_Bridge liquidity node was in the KG showing $120k pool depth but was never queried by the agent. The RiskConstraint:max_slippage was also available and would have contradicted the agent's 0% setting. The MEV_protection node flagged no protection on the canonical bridge.
